Find the cause before replacing parts

Record what changed, make one supported change at a time, and keep a way back.

Work through a specific symptom

A source-backed path for no display, persistent debug lights, memory and missing storage.

Read all checks
Before an internal check

Turn off the PC and disconnect its power. Follow the exact model manuals. Keep cooling installed for boot tests. Never open a PSU or substitute undocumented modular cables. Stop when a procedure or data-loss risk is unclear.

Start with what you can observe.

What can you observe?

Choose the symptom you can reproduce. This guide narrows the next check; it cannot identify a failed component remotely.

Your check record

    No automatic saving. Notes are never sent to this site’s server.

    The checks and their outcomes

    Read a single check or follow its linked next options. A persistent light narrows an investigation; it does not prove that a part is defective.

    Check the display path first

    Check the display path first

    Select the monitor input and check the cable. Use the graphics card output when relying on a discrete card; a motherboard output requires CPU graphics support.

    What to look for

    Look for the firmware screen or a change in the monitor’s signal indication.

    Keep a way back

    Return the monitor input or external cable to its previous position if this check changes nothing.

    The firmware screen is visible nowStill no signal; a debug light stays onStill no signal; no clear debug indication

    ASUS: no power, no boot or no display

    The display path changed the result

    The display path changed the result

    Record which input, output or cable restored the picture. This observation does not establish that every other component is healthy.

    What to look for

    Check that firmware recognizes the installed CPU, memory and storage.

    Observation recorded; further checks may remain.

    Continue the first-boot checklist

    ASUS: no power, no boot or no display

    Read the printed label, not only its color

    Read the printed label, not only its color

    During startup, LEDs may change in sequence. Use the exact board manual to interpret a light that remains on; labels and behavior vary.

    What to look for

    Identify the persistent label after the board’s documented initialization procedure.

    CPUDRAMVGABOOTI cannot identify it / it keeps cycling

    ASUS: motherboard Q-LED troubleshooting · MSI: motherboard boot and display checks

    Verify CPU support and power connections

    Verify CPU support and power connections

    With power disconnected before internal work, compare the exact CPU with the board’s CPU-support list and required BIOS. Check the CPU power plugs against the board and PSU manuals.

    What to look for

    A confirmed processor/BIOS match and documented required connections.

    Keep a way back

    Keep the original cables. Do not flash guessed firmware, mix modular PSU cables or remove the CPU as a first step.

    CPU or BIOS support is unresolvedSupported and plugs checked; still no display

    MSI: motherboard boot and display checks

    Test one documented memory configuration

    Test one documented memory configuration

    Disconnect power before reseating. Use one module in the manual’s recommended single-module slot. Give initialization the time documented for this board.

    What to look for

    A firmware screen, changed LED indication or the same failure. Record the module and slot used.

    Keep a way back

    Restore the recorded module/slot configuration with power disconnected. Stop if you cannot verify the seating or slot procedure.

    It reaches the firmware screenIt still stops at DRAMI cannot verify the slot or procedure

    ASUS: no power, no boot or no display · ASUS: motherboard Q-LED troubleshooting

    Check card seating, power and output

    Check card seating, power and output

    Disconnect power before checking card seating and required power plugs. Follow the exact GPU, board and PSU instructions. Confirm that the monitor cable uses the intended output.

    What to look for

    A firmware picture or a changed diagnostic indication after one documented check.

    Keep a way back

    Restore the original connection after a check that changes nothing. Never substitute a modular cable based on appearance.

    A picture appearsThe VGA indication remainsI need the correct instructions

    ASUS: no power, no boot or no display · ASUS: motherboard Q-LED troubleshooting

    Use the board’s minimal-POST procedure

    Use the board’s minimal-POST procedure

    Follow the manufacturer’s documented minimal configuration. Keep CPU cooling installed; retain a graphics card if the CPU has no usable integrated graphics. Disconnect power before removing internal parts.

    What to look for

    Observe whether the failure persists with only the documented required components.

    Keep a way back

    Reconnect removed devices one at a time, with power disconnected. Record which change alters the result.

    Firmware opens with the minimal setupIt still fails or I cannot verify the procedure

    MSI: motherboard boot and display checks

    Reconnect one item at a time

    Reconnect one item at a time

    A successful minimal setup narrows the investigation. Restore one recorded device or connection, then repeat the same boot check.

    What to look for

    Identify a repeatable change in behavior. A correlation is not proof that the last part is defective.

    Keep a way back

    Return to the last working documented configuration. Preserve your observations before seeking model-specific support.

    Observation recorded; further checks may remain.

    Check the exact parts and unresolved compatibility

    MSI: motherboard boot and display checks

    Which memory issue do you have?

    Which memory issue do you have?

    Record module part numbers, installed count, reported capacity and operating data rate before changing anything.

    Some installed capacity is missingThe operating rate is below the kit labelCrashes started after XMP / EXPO or a memory change
    Compare the operating setting with the profile

    Compare the operating setting with the profile

    Check the actual firmware data rate and exact kit profile. DDR data rate in MT/s is twice its clock frequency in MHz. Profile operation depends on the CPU, board, BIOS and module configuration.

    What to look for

    Distinguish a units mismatch or default setting from an unsupported configuration.

    Keep a way back

    Record current settings before changing them. Do not raise voltage or enable a profile without exact support instructions.

    It was a MHz versus MT/s units differenceIt is a default rate or support is uncertain

    Kingston: CAS latency and memory timings

    Return to a documented baseline

    Return to a documented baseline

    Use the board’s instructions to disable the optional memory profile or restore supported defaults. Record changed settings first; defaults can also affect boot and security settings.

    What to look for

    Repeat the same failing workload at the documented baseline.

    Keep a way back

    Keep the previous values and recovery instructions. Do not blindly clear CMOS or change unrelated settings.

    The workload is stable at defaultsIt still fails at defaultsI cannot safely access or change firmware

    Kingston: CAS latency and memory timings · ASUS: no power, no boot or no display

    Record the rate in the correct units

    Record the rate in the correct units

    For DDR, a 3,000 MHz memory clock corresponds to 6,000 MT/s. This unit conversion does not prove stability, capacity or a particular application result.

    Observation recorded; further checks may remain.

    Compare timing specifications

    Kingston: CAS latency and memory timings

    The optional profile is part of the investigation

    The optional profile is part of the investigation

    Keep the working baseline. Consult the exact board/CPU/kit support and BIOS notes before trying another configuration. Stability at defaults does not prove that the advertised profile is guaranteed on this system.

    Observation recorded; further checks may remain.

    Review memory compatibility checks

    Kingston: CAS latency and memory timings

    Record the working module and slot

    Record the working module and slot

    One working arrangement is useful evidence. It does not establish that another module is faulty. Reintroduce the remaining modules using the documented slot order and record each result.

    Observation recorded; further checks may remain.

    Check the full memory configuration

    ASUS: no power, no boot or no display

    Where is the drive missing?

    Where is the drive missing?

    Identify the drive by exact model and capacity. Firmware detection, a boot entry and a Windows drive letter are separate observations.

    Firmware does not list the driveFirmware sees it, but Windows File Explorer does notIt is listed but the PC will not boot from itI am not sure where it is missing
    Check the interface and documented slot rules

    Check the interface and documented slot rules

    Disconnect power before checking the connection. Verify the exact drive interface, supported slot and shared-port restrictions in the board manual; M.2 alone does not identify the interface.

    What to look for

    A supported connection and a repeatable firmware detection result.

    Keep a way back

    Restore the recorded slot/cable arrangement if a check changes nothing. Do not format a drive to solve firmware detection.

    The drive is now detectedA slot or interface restriction is unresolvedIt is still absent after documented checks

    ASUS: motherboard Q-LED troubleshooting

    Does the drive contain data you need?

    Does the drive contain data you need?

    Open Windows Disk Management to inspect the exact disk, without initializing, formatting or deleting anything yet.

    What to look for

    Confirm the disk identity and whether it has existing partitions or valuable data.

    Yes, or I am not certainIt is definitely a new empty drive

    Microsoft: initialize new disks and data precautions

    Preserve the data before repair

    Preserve the data before repair

    Stop before initialization, formatting or deletion. A missing letter or an uninitialized status does not make an existing disk safe to erase. Use documented troubleshooting or qualified recovery support.

    What to look for

    A backup or recovery plan before any destructive action.

    Next step: model-specific support.

    Read Microsoft’s disk troubleshooting

    Microsoft: initialize new disks and data precautions

    Follow the new-disk setup instructions

    Follow the new-disk setup instructions

    For a confirmed new empty drive, use Microsoft’s initialization and volume-creation instructions. Reconfirm the exact disk before applying any write operation.

    What to look for

    A configured volume and drive letter. Initialization and formatting are not a hardware-detection repair.

    Keep a way back

    There is no safe undo for erasing the wrong disk; stop if its identity or data status is uncertain.

    Next step: a documented manual procedure.

    Open Microsoft’s new-disk instructions

    Microsoft: initialize new disks and data precautions

    Verify the boot configuration without erasing data

    Verify the boot configuration without erasing data

    Record the firmware boot entries and the previous working storage configuration. A detected drive may lack the required boot entry; do not initialize it merely because Windows will not start.

    What to look for

    Model-specific recovery instructions that preserve existing data.

    Next step: model-specific support.

    Review Windows recovery options

    Microsoft: initialize new disks and data precautions

    Resolve the exact slot configuration

    Resolve the exact slot configuration

    Check the manual for your board revision and installed CPU. Shared lanes or disabled connections are conditional rules, not proof of a defective drive.

    Next step: verify the exact documentation.

    Start with the exact model’s manual

    Start with the exact model’s manual

    Find the motherboard model and revision, CPU, memory kit and GPU model. Use their official support pages for indicators, slots and procedures. Stop before an internal step you cannot verify.

    Next step: verify the exact documentation.

    Bring the recorded evidence to model-specific support

    Bring the recorded evidence to model-specific support

    Keep the symptom, exact models, firmware version, persistent indicator and checks already performed. Remaining possibilities need model-specific investigation; this guide has not proven a part defective.

    More diagnostic checklists

    Keep the starting state

    Record the application or game version, settings, driver version, recent hardware changes and the circumstances that reproduce the issue. Compare the same scene and workload after each change. A single utilization reading cannot diagnose every constraint.

    Use official drivers and exact support manuals. Never open a power supply, reuse undocumented modular cables, or use unofficial firmware and automatic driver-updater utilities.
